correctness.rationale: For each fixed finite \(p\ge1\), Kovalev Proposition 2.1 is reconstructed by conformal-strip subordination. The exact angular moment is converted into a positive deficit on \(x\in(0,1)\). Its \(x<a\) part is \(O(a)\); on \(x\ge a\) the uniform Taylor remainder integrates exactly to \(a\sqrt{1-a^2}\), and the leading kernel integrates to \(\log((1+\sqrt{1-a^2})/a)\). Thus \(1-N_p(r)^p=(4p/\pi^2)a\log(1/a)+O_p(a)\), and the \(p\)-th root plus \(1/r\) normalization gives coefficient \(4/\pi^2\) for every fixed finite \(p\). Strict near-boundary sign follows from logarithmic dominance. Fourier-Parseval separately checks \(p=2\) normalization; 12 finite checks corroborate only. The small-radius limit and continuity yield existence of a crossing for each \(p>p_{\mathbb R}\), not uniqueness.
